name: Luna 16
short_status: Success: returned 101 g of Mare Fecunditatis soil, 12 to 24 September 1970, the first robotic sample return from another world.
tagline: Soviet Union · Sample return · 1970 · The space race Success
stats: of lunar soil returned to Earth
sample return in history, and the first by a robot

facts.label: Lunar orbit insertion
facts.value: 17 September 1970, into a 111 km circular orbit; perilune later lowered to 15.1 km

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 20 September 1970, 05:18 UT, Mare Fecunditatis; first landing made in the lunar night (Sun had set about 60 hours earlier)

facts.label: Sample
facts.value: 101 grams from a single 35 cm drill core; the drill stopped after hitting hard rock at that depth

facts.label: Surface stay / ascent
facts.value: 26 hours 25 minutes on the surface; ascent stage lifted off 21 September 1970 at 07:43 UT

facts.label: Earth return
facts.value: 24 September 1970; ballistic reentry with no mid-course corrections, capsule landed about 80 km SE of Dzhezkazgan, Kazakhstan (NSSDCA gives 03:26 UT)

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: Ye-8-5 bus, 3.96 m tall; 1,880 kg dry landed mass, 5,600 to 5,750 kg fueled at launch; return capsule 50 cm diameter, 39 kg

facts.label: Sample exchange with NASA
facts.value: March 1973: NASA traded 3 g each of Apollo 16 and Apollo 17 material for Luna 16 and Luna 20 samples

facts.label: Only legal private sale of Moon rocks
facts.value: Three Luna 16 fragments (~0.2 g), originally gifted to Sergei Korolev's widow, sold at Sotheby's for $855,000 on 29 November 2018

timeline: 05:18 UT: Soft-lands in Mare Fecunditatis, the first landing in lunar darkness
Drill penetrates 35 cm, collects 101 g, seals it in the return capsule
07:43 UT: Ascent stage lifts off the Moon after 26 h 25 min on the surface
Capsule lands ~80 km SE of Dzhezkazgan, Kazakhstan, completing the first robotic sample return
NASA and the USSR exchange samples: 6 g of Apollo material for Luna 16 and Luna 20 soil
Three Luna 16 fragments sell at Sotheby's for $855,000, still the only legal private sale of Moon rocks
